apiContracts: GET-only; optional q parameter must be at most 80 characters; longer queries return an empty array before database access; accepted searches escape LIKE wildcard characters; max 50 matching authors or 100 directory authors; aggregate output only.
dataEntities: No new entities. Aggregate data is derived only from novels that are published and have rights_status in original, public_domain, licensed or authorized.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: Reuses existing novels and author display-name fields. No schema changes.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: Existing /author/:name profile URLs and GET /api/public-authors remain compatible; the endpoint is hardened without changing its response fields.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Revert the page, renderer, navigation and route additions together. The hardened read-only API can remain or be reverted independently; no data repair is required.

uiLifecycle.ssrBehavior: The Worker serves a dedicated authors.html shell at /authors and applies the static canonical SEO metadata.
uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: The canonical localized app shell renders the searchable directory, uses the public aggregate API and links to existing public author profiles.
uiLifecycle.servedBundleParity: public/app.js and public/app-17.23.0.js must remain byte-identical; authors-page.js loads before the versioned application bundle.

privacySecurity.authentication: The directory and aggregate endpoint are public and do not require a session.
privacySecurity.authorization: The endpoint exposes only author display names and aggregate counts derived from published, rights-eligible novels.
privacySecurity.ownerScoping: No account IDs, emails, private profile fields or unpublished works are returned.
privacySecurity.csrf: GET-only read surface; no state mutation.
privacySecurity.rateAndSizeLimits: Search query is limited to 80 characters; overlong queries return an empty array without a database query; result rows are capped at 50 for search and 100 for directory.
privacySecurity.rightsAndPrivacy: Only original, public-domain, licensed or authorized published novels contribute to the public directory.

unit: test-public-author-discovery.mjs validates route, rights filtering, 80-character pre-query guard, escaped literal LIKE search, bounds, safe rendering, SEO and bundle parity.
integration: Desktop and mobile navigation link to /authors; client route renders a searchable author directory and links to existing public author profiles.
The API rejects non-GET methods and returns bounded aggregates only.

test-worker-public-author-discovery.mjs starts the actual Worker against fresh local D1 and verifies method guards, aggregate projection, rights filtering, literal wildcard searches, overlong-query rejection and result bounds.
isolation: Anonymous directory access exposes no account identity or private creator fields.
Unpublished and rights-ineligible novels do not contribute to author counts or recorded reads.
test-worker-account-reader-isolation.mjs verifies anonymous author discovery exposes aggregate fields only and excludes unpublished or rights-ineligible works.

Verify the 14 supported interface languages, RTL direction and desktop/mobile navigation.
Verify public/app.js and public/app-17.23.0.js are byte-identical.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert the author directory page, page renderer, route/navigation wiring, SEO and route/matrix records as one feature slice.
rollback.dataRollbackOrForwardRepair: No database migration or data mutation exists.
monitoringSignals: Public author endpoint error rate and response size

collisionReview.duplicateRoutes: /authors is absent from the canonical route registry before this change; /author/:name remains the existing individual profile route.
collisionReview.duplicateEntities: No new entity; aggregate uses existing novels.author.
collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: catalog owns the aggregate projection; experience-shell owns the page and application shell; platform-kernel owns Worker/SEO integration; platform-quality owns tests; platform-architecture owns route/method/auth inventories and ADR; platform-integrator serializes shared surfaces.

changeSummary: Reconstructs the missing public author directory as a bounded, localized feature slice on the canonical integration root. Reuses the existing public-author API but hardens search and aggregates, adds /authors routing and SEO/sitemap coverage, integrates desktop/mobile navigation, and synchronizes the editable and served app bundles.
acceptanceCriteria: /authors resolves to a dedicated authors.html shell and appears in the canonical route registry and static sitemap.
Desktop and mobile navigation expose the directory in all fourteen supported locales.
The client renders author names as text and links safely to existing /author/:name profiles.
The API is GET-only, rejects q values longer than 80 characters before database access, escapes LIKE wildcard characters literally, and limits output to 50/100 rows.
Only published novels with original, public_domain, licensed or authorized rights contribute to aggregates.
Views are coalesced to zero and invalid ratings outside 1–10 are excluded from aggregates.
No private creator or account fields are returned.
SEO metadata is indexable and canonical; app.js and app-17.23.0.js are byte-identical.
Route, API method, authorization and sitemap inventories match the implemented behavior.
All six exact-head integration workflows pass; no production deployment or D1 migration is performed.
